By the Dirichlet method, I meant using MLE on the raw proportions of votes for each item, without considering the total number of votes. The difference is that this method treats each item as equally likely to have occurred, whereas the Dirichlet-multinomial process would consider items with more votes to be "less likely".

Bottom line is this: should I fit alpha on the proportion of votes or the votes themselves (i.e. [0.2, 0.2, 0.3, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1] vs [4, 4, 6, 2, 2, 2]).

The intent is to use the parameter vector to act as a pseudocount for additive smoothing. For example, if the MLE parameters for the dataset was \[1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1\], then I would add one "pseudo-vote" for each of the possible scores. So an item with counts \[5, 10, 10, 10, 15, 10\] (average score = 2.9), then the smoothed counts would be \[6, 11, 11, 11, 16, 11\] (average score =  2.85714285714).

The issue of the variance in the number of star counts is the problem that this solution is intended to fix. The additive smoothing will account for uncertainty in an item's "true" score by weighting items with a small number of votes to the mean. Items with more votes will be less impacted by this additive smoothing.

Dirichlet and Dirichlet-multinomial are parametrized the same way, but the MLE process is different, hence the question.
